title: >=3.2-dev8: Hanging stats socket with cpu-policy group-by-cluster
body:
### Detailed Description of the Problem

Regarding https://github.com/orgs/haproxy/discussions/2901#discussioncomment-12934325

Our config and systems were unmodified and are running very stable for quite some time with 3.1.6 (except one rare but already fixed issue in 3.1.7) and 3.2-dev (currently -dev11, started with dev0) and never had *this* problem.
When adding `cpu-policy group-by-cluster` to the global section, HAProxy becomes unresponsive / blocking after some time but it seems only for the stats socket. It seems to still serve traffic. Reload doesn't help, only restart.

It is unclear yet what's triggering this issue. It's not immediately and it takes some minutes (usually <10m). A reload isn't required to trigger it it seems.

### Expected Behavior

Working stats socket

### Steps to Reproduce the Behavior

1. 3.2-dev11
2. cpu-policy group-by-cluster in the global section
3. some magic
4. echo help | socat /path/to/socket stdio
5. Get no response and/or blocking connections to the socket (not socat tho) and high CPU usage


### Do you have any idea what may have caused this?

Somehow related to cpu-policy group-by-cluster

### Do you have an idea how to solve the issue?

_No response_

### What is your configuration?

```haproxy
N/A
```

comments.body:
OK thanks for the info. So if you say it usually takes less than 10mn, we could imagine that the python script passes at most once or twice before it happens, so maybe it manages to trigger the issue by dumping such stats and info.

Before you spend a lot of time bisecting, I'd suggest to instead try to manually configure the groups like the cpu-policy does it:
```
    thread-groups 8
    cpu-map 1/1-16 0-7   64-71
    cpu-map 2/1-16 8-15  72-79
    cpu-map 3/1-16 16-23 80-87
    cpu-map 4/1-16 24-31 88-95
    cpu-map 5/1-16 32-39 96-103
    cpu-map 6/1-16 40-47 104-111
    cpu-map 7/1-16 48-55 112-119
    cpu-map 8/1-16 56-63 120-127
```

Logically it should reproduce the issue. My fear is that we could have a deeper bug somewhere in file descriptor management or any such thing when it comes to thread groups, and that could be more easily triggered by your setup than others.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: OK that allows us to narrow it quite a bit more. I really suspect that an event is being ignored and I don't understand why. And seeing fd_grab_tgid() appear here doesn't amuse me. It's one of the super-sensitive parts of the thread-group code. I'm suspecting that the sharing of outgoing connections between thread groups could have woken up a subtle race. Could you please try with `tune.idle-pool.shared off` in the global section ? It will stop sharing idle conns between servers and will make sure FDs don't switch from one thread to the other. It's indeed possible that a precise timing happens between the FD used (or released?) by the CLI and one used by an idle conn that changed thread.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Ah got it! And it can trivially be reproduced with `bind ... shards 1` on a line. It just happens that since the introduction of group-based shards, we now use them by default and there's no bounding between groups by default outside of the stats socket. I suspect that your script might re-establish a connection just before finishing consuming the old one, leaving a short window where a connection still exists, encouraging the accept's load balancing to bounce the connection to another thread. The code just forgets to transfer the nbconn when switching to another group (needed because technically speaking it's another listener).

Now I can't break it anymore (including in http with shards 1). I've just merged the patch above (f1064c7). Christian, many thanks once again for this great observation and all the details. It could have lived long without your precious help!
